A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–E support reliable comparison. V2 additionally includes acknowledgements and a conference checklist.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original Monte Carlo results and distributional treatment-effect estimates using Oregon Health Insurance Experiment data, including Figures 2–4.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original simulation results and reports revised Oregon application estimates and uncertainty measures in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The regression-adjusted LDTE estimator, nuisance functions, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V2 formalizes LPTE, which was already estimated in v1. The Oregon cross-fitting change is an experimental configuration change, not a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four-stratum, 20-covariate nonlinear simulation and Oregon emergency-department-visit application. LDTE and LPTE were already evaluated in v1; their coverage is not expanded.

E2.justification: Both versions compare gradient-boosting adjustment with unadjusted and linearly adjusted estimators in simulations, and with unadjusted estimates in Oregon. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 and Figure 4 change the reported Oregon cross-fitting configuration from 2 folds to 5 folds. The sample size of 17,021, covariates, and outcome thresholds remain unchanged. Simulation settings, including 2-fold cross-fitting, are retained.

E4.justification: No new ablation, robustness condition, error analysis, or additional case study appears. Figure 3 retains the same sample-size analysis. The Oregon application addresses the same questions, with setting and numerical updates rather than an added diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 simulation replications, 95% confidence intervals, and 500 bootstrap replications for Oregon. Appendix D retains the analytical variance estimator and bootstrap algorithm. Revised standard-error values do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Section 6.2 and Figure 4 revise the Oregon estimates: the reported zero-visit effect changes from approximately -11 percentage points to -9, with adjusted standard error changing from 4.5 to 4.2 points. The five-visit effect changes from approximately +2 points (SE 1) to +1.7 (SE 0.8). Precision-reduction ranges also change. These accompany revised cross-fitting settings; simulation results and the main qualitative application findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a formal LPTE definition for outcome intervals and states how LDTE theoretical results extend through indicator substitution. V1 used LPTE without this formal treatment. The principal assumptions, theorems, and Appendix C proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: regression-adjusted distributional inference under covariate-adaptive randomization and noncompliance, asymptotic normality, semiparametric efficiency, and empirical usefulness.

C2.justification: The Oregon discussion qualifies the previously uniform precision-gain account by acknowledging increased LPTE standard errors at zero through three visits. The conclusion adds a specific future direction involving non-asymptotic frameworks from Su et al. Existing IV assumptions and binary-treatment limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E replaces the code-access placeholder with a repository reference and adds access information for the dte-adj Python package. Hardware and covariate documentation are retained. The new checklist asserts detailed reproducibility information, but the supplied PDF adds no corresponding hyperparameter or execution-time specifications.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hirata et al. (2025), Byambadalai et al. (2025), and two Su et al. (2023) references. It distinguishes prior distributional work under full compliance and identifies non-asymptotic extensions as future work. Oka et al.’s publication update represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgements and a NeurIPS checklist, updates front matter, corrects the appendix description, and makes localized explanatory and application edits. The main narrative, section sequence, and technical appendix organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with different axis ranges, tick spacing, and panel proportions. Figures 2 and 3 retain their plots but gain expanded captions. Front matter and pagination change, while the existing tables and overall visual organization remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: V2 fills limited documentation gaps through the LPTE definition, concrete code/package references, and clearer figure captions. It also acknowledges nonuniform precision gains in Oregon. These improve clarity and transparency while the core theory and simulation evidence remain stable. The revised application settings do not establish a performance improvement, and checklist assertions exceed the implementation details supplied in the PDF.
